Omarchy has a built-in way to set simple reminders based on a countdown timer and with a message. You can do this via `Super + Ctrl + R`
You can quickly access the date and time, battery status, and current weather using the hotkey notices.
Hit `Super + Ctrl + PrtScr` to select a region on the screen for text extraction. The tesseract open source OCR model will then quickly convert that selection into text
Once installed, you dictate by holding down `F9` or by toggling with `Super + Ctrl + X`, and the dictated text will appear in the focused input area.
you can also control it through the `omarchy` CLI. This is particularly helpful when you're having an AI agent work with you on customization or configuration.
we fully support _Ghostty_, _Foot_, and _Kitty_ as options as well. Pick your preference under _Install > Terminal_ in the Omarchy menu.
[Neovim](https://neovim.io/) is a modern implementation of the vi editor... it's a bit of a superpower once you learn even just a subset of the incredibly deep key command set.
Omarchy ships with [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai/) and [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview) as the default agent harnesses for programmers.
We have VSCode, Cursor, Zed, Sublime Text, and Helix listed there... Theme matching is offered for `VSCode`, `Cursor`, `VSCodium`, `Helix`, and `Zed`.
Omarchy supports setting up a whole host of development environments through the _Install > Development_ section of the Omarchy Menu
[fzf](https://junegunn.github.io/fzf/) gives you fuzzy finding of files via the `ff` alias... [Zoxide](https://github.com/ajeetdsouza/zoxide) is a replacement for cd.
On first boot, Omarchy invites you to set up a default agent. Pick your favorite, sign in, and put it to work on your computer.
When an app crashes, click the notification to send your agent on the case. It can examine the crash dump, diagnose what went wrong, and help report the bug.
Omarchy ships with skills to help your agent make apps, plugins, and themes. Describe what you want, try what it builds, and share it with everyone.
Neovim is the default, with VSCode, Cursor, Zed, Sublime Text, Helix, Vim, and Emacs ready to install. Pick your favorite and make it the system-wide default.
Install Ruby on Rails, Laravel, Node.js, and a long list of other development environments from the Omarchy menu. Mise handles language versions, so each project can use what it needs.
Foot is the fast, lightweight default. Prefer Alacritty, Ghostty, or Kitty? All four are integrated, and switching your default keeps the same keyboard shortcuts working.
Omarchy comes ready for Steam, RetroArch, and a whole world of gaming. Graphics drivers and configuration, including NVIDIA on supported hardware, are sorted during installation.
Choose _Install > Windows_ from the Omarchy menu. Hardware virtualization brings near-native CPU performance for Office and everyday work, with a shared clipboard and a folder for moving files
Bring a Windows 11 Pro license valid for a VM. Run `omarchy windows key` to retrieve your machine's original key (this only works on Pro, not Home licenses).
All of Omarchy running in a virtual machine, so you can get a taste first.
Write the ISO to a USB stick and answer five questions. It hands back a finished desktop.
The manual also covers [dual booting beside Windows](/manual/dual-boot-install/) and [unattended installs](/manual/unattended-installs/).
A theme restyles the whole system at once: terminal, bar, notifications, wallpaper. Pick one and this site wears it too.
You can find even more themes on the extra themes page or even make your own theme.
Ladybird is great, but Omarchy is a weird choice... I don't see the value in yet another flavor-of-the-week Linux distro. Even sponsoring Arch directly would make more sense here.
I cannot for the life of me understand the Omarchy hype. The Linux community has been theming their distribution installs for decades. What distinguishes this from that?

The hype around Omarchy is just insane... you have to download a 7GB ISO file (in the name of 'good UX') that ships with Zoom, Spotify, Hey, Basecamp, Steam, Minecraft... but you still end up using the same package mirrors (arch's).
Timely sponsorship, downloading the Omarchy 3 ISO last week sat at about 600 KiB/s. Appreciated!
I don't know, Omarchy's team really don't care if you're complaining... I'm sure with the $10M cash chest the security will just improve over time.

A friend has been urging me to install Omarchy for months. I've finally caved in after a horrible experience with highly-praised CachyOS. All I can say is, I understand the hype. It works. The install is uncomplicated... Installing software is easy and lightning-fast.
Apparently the Omarchy plugin ecosystem is also a free for all like the Arch AUR, except the audience includes people who are new to Linux and less likely to understand the risks.
Bash injection using video Titles!? ...There are bangers like video title bash injection or all notifications being able to run arbitrary bash on your machine.
I want to love Omarchy but replacing the boot splash screen with its logo is rough, I wish there was a clear way to disable that.
The real story with Omarchy is Hyprland... Hyprland itself comes with such nice defaults that it isn't surprising at all that it's getting as much attention as it is.

Well, this 'not distro' software that takes over your whole computer when you boot the ISO and install it has been the greatest out-of-the box Linux experience for me... Now I am on the edge of making my work laptop dual boot it.

I've tried to setup Arch with Hyprland like 3 times on my own and with the most popular dot files. It was terrible, frustrating and things broke all the time. Omarchy fixed that and I can't recommend it enough.

I checked it out slightly more and noticed that the omarchy installation script enables the chaotic.cx repo... Omarchy enables all this silently with pacman -U --noconfirm. This... constitutes a pretty bad supply side attack vector.

Cons: Its designed to be a single user setup... So for a shared pc its not ideal - the way its currently configured I think you need to run the omarchy bash install script for each user and also update individually for each one.
